The test image shows a large, round gall-like structure on a corn plant with:
- Dark brown-black rough outer surface (partially ruptured)
- White/cream inner structures visible at the base
- Growing from the stalk/node area

This strongly suggests **Common_smut** or possibly **Head_smut**. Let me check reference images.

Common_smut reference shows green/pale galls early, Head_smut shows fibrous masses at the ear/tassel. The test image has a large round gall with dark outer surface and white inner structures — consistent with Common_smut. Let me check a few more classes to confirm.
Crazy_top shows leafy proliferations (not galls). Ear_rots_Diplodia shows cottony white mold on kernels. Neither matches. Let me view 2 more to meet the minimum requirement.

Neither Gibberella ear rot (pink mold on husks) nor Common rust (small leaf pustules) match at all.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a large, round, fist-sized gall on a corn stalk/ear node with:
- **Dark brown-black rough outer surface** — mature spore mass, partially ruptured
- **White/cream rounded inner structures** — early-stage gall tissue still intact at the base
- **Large, irregular mass** replacing normal plant tissue at the node

This matches **Common_smut** precisely:
- Galls form on any above-ground meristematic tissue (stalk nodes, ears)
- The white inner structures = early-stage pale/turgid gall tissue
- The dark outer surface = mature membrane rupturing to expose dark spore masses
- The size and round shape are characteristic

**Head_smut** was ruled out — it shows fibrous, thread-like masses replacing ear/tassel structures, not the large round gall seen here. The Common_smut reference images show the same round globular galls in exactly this progression.
